Subject: FinPath onboarding — model shortlist & runtime sizing check-in

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our notes, attached is a first-pass model shortlist and token-volume worksheet that maps your three prioritized flows (invoice ingestion Q&A, payment reconciliation assistant, and reconciliation summary emails) to context-length needs and rough per-request token expectations.

Key asks from us to refine sizing:
- Typical prompt length (raw text) and expected reply length for each flow (best guess is fine).
- % of requests that need full-document context vs. short queries (we used 15% full-doc in the attached sheet).
- Peak concurrency window (e.g., 09:00–11:00 PST daily, or specific days).

Initial findings in the attachment:
- Shortlist: a 3-tier approach (high-throughput small model, balanced mid, long-context large model).
- Context guidance: for the reconciliation assistant we recommend preserving a 3–4k token window unless the documents are heavily preprocessed (extracted key fields).
- Token estimate (current best guess): ~1.3M accept-rate tokens/day with a 2x peak multiplier (see finpath_token_estimates_v1.csv).

Can you confirm the above guesses, or send the raw sample sizes you mentioned? If that works, Monica and I can put together a 45-minute sizing deep-dive and a proposed Mutual Action Plan with suggested Dedicated vs Hosted split.

Attachments: finpath_model_shortlist_v1.pdf, finpath_token_estimates_v1.csv, mutual-action-plan-finpath.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — quickly read the attachments. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Context: Invoice ingestion Q&A will often need the full invoice (avg ~850 tokens) plus the last 2–3 messages of a thread for context (~200 tokens). For some exceptions (large vendor packets) we may need up to ~3.5k tokens but those are rare (~3% of requests).
2) Expected reply size: most replies are concise (50–120 tokens); reconciliation summary emails can be longer (200–400 tokens).
3) Peak: Our busiest hours are 08:30–10:00 EST (daily, Monday–Friday). Typical concurrency today during that window is ~35 simultaneous users; on billing days it spikes higher.

Main concern: latency — our SLAs are human-interactive (sub-800ms ideally for short flows). If choosing a larger context model adds 400–600ms, that may impact adoption for certain flows.

Happy to join the sizing deep-dive next week.

—Liam

On Mon, Aug 11, 2025 at 09:44 AM Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@finpath.io> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — quickly read the attachments. A couple clarifications from our side: 
> 
> 1) Context: Invoice ingestion Q&A will often need the full invoice (avg ~850 tokens) plus the last 2–3 messages of a thread for context (~200 tokens). For some exceptions (large vendor packets) we may need up to ~3.5k tokens but those are rare (~3% of requests).
> 2) Expected reply size: most replies are concise (50–120 tokens); reconciliation summary emails can be longer (200–400 tokens).
> 3) Peak: Our busiest hours are 08:30–10:00 EST (daily, Monday–Friday). Typical concurrency today during that window is ~35 simultaneous users; on billing days it spikes higher.

Thanks for the details — this helps tighten the estimates. A few recommendations from the onboarding/CS side:

- Model shortlist rationale (high-level):
  * Throughput model (rwd-7B-fast): low latency, low cost for short queries (recommended for Q&A and high-frequency lookups).
  * Balanced model (rwd-13B-balance): middle ground for mixed-length requests where we care about accuracy but still need reasonable latency.
  * Long-context model (rwd-34B-windowed): preserves up to 8k tokens; use for full-document summarization and the rare >3k token cases.

- Context strategy:
  * Prefix extraction: extract invoice key-fields server-side (vendor, line-items summary) and pass the parsed summary as a prefix for short flows — this reduces the need to keep full doc tokens in the prompt for routine Q&A.
  * KV/prefix cache: for multi-turn workflows keep the KV cache active for 60–90s in the session to avoid re-streaming the same context across rapid back-and-forths.

- Token-volume sensitivity (rough numbers, internal):
  * Baseline mix: 70% short Q&A (prompt ~300 tokens, reply ~90 tokens), 27% mid-length (prompt+context ~1.1k, reply ~220), 3% long (avg roundtrip 3.6k + 300 reply).
  * Daily token estimate (based on your ~35 concurrent and expected throughput): ~1.1–1.5M tokens/day. Peak hour multiplier: 2.2x.
  * Cost impact: moving 15% of traffic from small->balanced model increases per-token compute cost ~1.8x; using long-context model for even 3% can disproportionately raise peak GPU footprints because of sequence length scaling.

Recommendations / next steps before the deep-dive:
- Please share a small sample (10–20 anonymized invoices + 10 example Q&A sessions) so we can validate tokenization patterns and refine the shortlist.
- We'll prepare two variant MAPlists for you: Hosted-first (min infra, uses caching + batching) and Dedicated-lite (reserved capacity for peak windows).

I can present the model tradeoffs on the call next Tue/Thu — Ben, can you confirm availability? Marissa, I'll call out implications for pricing and committed capacity.

Best,
Monica Patel

Liam — quick note from pricing/legal side as we prepare the MAP: 

- For the hosted-first option we can cap burst to 4x the committed baseline for the first 90 days while we gather telemetry. That gives you breathing room on heavy billing days while avoiding an immediate dedicated commit.
- If you want sub-800ms P99 on the high-frequency flows, we'll likely need a Dedicated-lite pool for those routes (we've modeled a 2-GPU pool doing the small/fast model with autoscaling headroom).

If you can confirm target P99 latency and a soft monthly token budget range, I'll produce a pricing sketch that pairs the two MAP variants Monica mentioned.
